terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: all-in-one solar street lamp: galvanised pole, tilted photovoltaic panel and a flat LED lamp box on a short arm
motionPotential: none - bolted to a foundation; the panel is aimed once at installation
objectClass.notes: The all-in-one solar unit that has appeared on new provincial roads over the last decade. The plate is square-framed at aspect 0.851 against the declared 0.293, so it carries the fixture and not the assembly proportions; the declared 1.35 x 4.6 x 0.75 m envelope governs.

reasoning: Four drawn parts: the tapered pole, the bolted baseplate, the tilted solar panel and the LED lamp box.
No holding-down bolts: the large class ceiling is 4 draw calls and the four parts above use all of them. The bolts are the cheapest thing to drop on a 4.6 m prop and the omission is recorded.
The panel's TILT is what gives this prop its declared depth and most of its width; it is carried on the component's transform.rotation, not baked into a sweep.
No moving parts, so one root pivot and no sockets.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate; sub-structure carried as localFeatures because each component costs one of only four draw calls.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: A 0.92 x 0.74 m PV panel raked 0.30 rad, overhanging -X above the lamp head.
An aluminium frame proud of the cell laminate on all four sides.
Pale inter-cell lines over the dark blue wafer, as a post-construction tile spanning 0.55 m.
A flat slab head on the opposite side of the pole from the panel and below it.
A flared foot and a taper from r 0.070 to r 0.038 over the shaft.
Four triangular gussets welded up the pole from its baseplate.
A strut triangulating the panel back to the shaft.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: The pole section is polygonal in the plate; built octagonal as the sector standard. Confidence 0.7.
The far side of the pole, panel and lamp box is mirrored; the single view cannot show it. Confidence 0.85.
The panel's tilt angle is read off the plate at roughly 20 degrees; the exact angle is a siting choice rather than a property of the product. Confidence 0.6.
The battery box some variants carry under the panel is NOT visible in this plate and is not built. Confidence 0.8.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsNote: All intake unknowns are RESOLVED; each has a chosen answer and a stated confidence in resolvedUnknowns and in spec.assumptions. Nothing here blocks implementation, and the ones a second view would settle are not resolvable from a single plate by any amount of further analysis.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: the panel reads tilted and dominant
pole rendered luma against the measured 186, panel against 110-123
turntable hole gate at all four azimuths
antiShallowSpecRules: Every identity-defining detail in the inventory maps to a named localFeature, a vertexPaint region or a repetitionSystem - never to prose alone.
Every material carries a measured crop as textureless evidence.
Every geometric figure is measured off the plate, measured off the proxy band table, or derived from the declared envelope, and says which.
mustNotDo: Do not take proportion from the plate or the proxy.
Do not level the panel; the tilt is the declared depth and most of the declared width.
Do not lift the panel's albedo toward grey to clear the hole gate - hold it on chroma.
Do not add bolts; the draw-call ceiling is already met.
Do not let the lamp box share a plane with the panel's lower edge.
qualityContract.depthRationale: FIVE components across two material layers: the pole, panel and lamp head as macro, the baseplate and panel mount as meso. Seven micro-feature groups -- pole taper, base gussets, base bolts, the tilted panel, its framed laminate, the diagonal strut and the lamp box.

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Overall silhouette and the declared envelope
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Measured bbox must be 1.35 x 4.60 x 0.75 m within the asset's 10% tolerance.

featureReviewTargets.name: Tilted photovoltaic panel
featureReviewTargets.criteria: The panel must be a RAKED framed laminate overhanging one side, with a visible aluminium frame and a cell grid. A bare flat plate fails -- that is what the previous build shipped.

featureReviewTargets.name: Flat LED lamp box
featureReviewTargets.criteria: The LED head must be a SEPARATE volume from the panel, below it and on the opposite side of the pole. The asset notes make that arrangement the identity of the prop.

featureReviewTargets.name: Material response and the hole gate
featureReviewTargets.criteria: The pole must stay bright (measured 186, the brightest pole in the kit) and the panel dark but SATURATED - it holds the hole gate on chroma, not luma. No surface may render near the ~58 backdrop.

featureReviewTargets.name: Tapered faceted pole
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Section narrows monotonically and reads faceted, not round.

lookDevTargets.keyLightIntent: Hemisphere light plus three directionals, ACES tone mapping, no environment map.
lookDevTargets.materialSeparation: galvanised pole 186 / panel 110-123 in measured plate luma - the widest material separation of any prop in this lighting set.
lookDevTargets.holeGateFloor: No surface may render at or near the ~58 backdrop luma at any turntable azimuth, including the back-lit 180 frame which renders at ~0.55 of painted luma.
lookDevTargets.notes: Metalness is held below 1.0 on every metal because there is no environment map to reflect.

actionReadiness.notes: Explodable and clickable as four named parts. Not articulated and not breakable.

assumptions: The pole section is polygonal in the plate; built octagonal as the sector standard. Confidence 0.7.
The far side of the pole, panel and lamp box is mirrored; the single view cannot show it. Confidence 0.85.
The panel tilt is about 20 degrees, read off the plate; the exact angle is a siting choice rather than a property of the product.
Holding-down bolts are NOT built: the large class allows four draw calls and the four drawn parts use them all.
The panel's cell grid is not textured: it is a printed pattern at a scale a viewer cannot resolve from a 4.6 m lamp.
No battery box is built - none is visible in this plate.
Metalness is authored below a physical 1.0 on the steel because the harness carries no environment map.

coordinateFrame.originPolicy: base-center: the origin sits at the centre of the baseplate footprint on the ground plane (y=0).

silhouette.derivation: Measured bbox 1.340 x 4.546 x 0.716 m against the declared 1.35 x 4.6 x 0.75 -- within 1% on width, 1.2% on height and 4.5% on depth. Width is the panel's -X overhang plus the lamp head's +X; depth is the raked panel, the only thing on the prop that can set it.
silhouette.notes: The plate is square-framed at aspect 0.851 against the declared 0.293. The panel's tilt is what produces most of the declared width and the full height.

componentTree.name: Tapered steel pole with base gussets
componentTree.topologyRationale: A tapered lathe with four welded gussets. The previous build was a smooth pipe with neither, and the gussets are what read as a bolted structural post rather than a tube pushed into a plate.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Origin base-center, +Y up. A 10-segment lathe flaring to r 0.088 at the plate and tapering to r 0.038 at 4.36 m, with four triangular gussets over 0.19-0.51 m.

localFeatures.description: A flare at the foot and a taper from r 0.070 to r 0.038 over the shaft, read off the plate's silhouette.
Four triangular gussets welded up the pole from its baseplate, as the plate shows.

componentTree.notes: Galvanised #9ea5a6 with shaded steel #848b8c as a vertex colour, plus a bloom-and-rust tile -- the plate's foot is heavily rust-stained.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Galvanised steel carrying its shaded plates and the pale lamp head as vertex colours, with bloom and rust as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.name: Bolted square baseplate
componentTree.topologyRationale: A distinct fabricated part sharing the pole's material.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 0.32 m square plate 26 mm thick with four bolts inset 52 mm.

localFeatures.description: Four bolts at the plate corners.

componentTree.notes: Smaller than the road columns' plates -- this is a 4.6 m post.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Galvanised steel carrying its shaded plates and the pale lamp head as vertex colours, with bloom and rust as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.name: Tilted PV panel in its aluminium frame
componentTree.topologyRationale: A separate material because a PV laminate is neither steel nor paint, and the asset notes make the panel and the head SEPARATE VOLUMES at the right relative sizes the identity of this prop.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 0.92 x 0.74 m frame 32 mm thick raked 0.30 rad, with the cell laminate inset 55 mm on all four sides and standing 14 mm below the frame's top.

localFeatures.description: Raked 0.30 rad and overhanging -X, the widest thing on the prop and above the lamp head -- which is the arrangement the asset notes call the identity.
An aluminium frame standing proud of the cell laminate on all four sides, so the two never share a plane, with the cell grid as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.notes: Panel 0.92 x 0.74 rather than the notes' rough 1.0 x 0.6: the DECLARED ENVELOPE is 1.35 x 4.6 x 0.75 and the panel is the only thing that can set the depth -- at 0.6 the measured depth came out 0.659, 12% under.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: A dark blue cell laminate in a pale aluminium frame, the cell grid carried as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.name: Panel mounting bar and diagonal strut
componentTree.topologyRationale: Without the strut the panel reads as a plate balanced on a stick, and the plate shows it clearly.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 0.62 m bar under the panel carrying its rake, and a 0.44 m strut rotated -0.46 rad back to the shaft.

localFeatures.description: A strut triangulating the panel back to the shaft.

componentTree.notes: Same galvanised material as the pole.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Galvanised steel carrying its shaded plates and the pale lamp head as vertex colours, with bloom and rust as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.name: Flat LED head on its arm
componentTree.topologyRationale: A SEPARATE volume from the panel, below it and on the opposite side of the pole. The asset notes make exactly that the identity, and a head merged into the panel assembly would lose it.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 0.24 m arm and a 0.40 x 0.07 x 0.30 m slab head with a darker lens plate under it.

localFeatures.description: A flat slab head on the OPPOSITE side of the pole from the panel and 0.64 m below it, with a darker lens plate on its underside.

componentTree.notes: Head #b9bdba over the galvanised material, its lens plate #848b8c.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Galvanised steel carrying its shaded plates and the pale lamp head as vertex colours, with bloom and rust as a post-construction tile.

materials.name: Hot-dip galvanised steel

albedo.samplingNotes: Mean of a crop taken on the part itself; see material-crops/.

evidence: The plate's pole, gussets, baseplate, mounting bar and lamp head are one continuous galvanised finish with heavy rust staining at the foot.
Luma 162 sits well clear of the 55.5-60.5 window that gatecrop's alpha key erases, so no lift was needed.

roughness.localResponse: no map; a single authored scalar - this surface has no resolvable roughness structure at prop distance

ambientOcclusion.notes: Darken seams, joints and recessed features.

localOverrides.description: Dirt and rust at the foot as a vertex-colour axis-band (y -0.05..0.45, softness 0.45) authored at #A79A88, close to the measured #a69f94 - this one needs almost no lift because the surrounding steel is already bright.

shaderNotes: MeshStandardMaterial is sufficient: no clearcoat, sheen or transmission is observed.
Never alias albedo into roughness; both are authored scalars, not maps.
Metalness is authored BELOW a physical raw-metal 1.0 on purpose - see notes.
materials.notes: Metalness 0.35, matching the other galvanised posts in this kit.

materials.name: Photovoltaic panel

albedo.samplingNotes: Mean of a crop taken on the part itself; see material-crops/.

evidence: The plate's panel is the only cool blue on the prop, its cells clearly gridded by pale inter-cell lines and bounded by a bright aluminium frame.
Textureless is NOT declared here: the cell grid is the one identity-defining texture on the prop, and the tile is bound AFTER construction so no procedural set is synthesised.
The tile spans 0.55 m rather than 0.16: at 0.16 it repeated six times across the panel and its bands became ~48 stripes, which read as a venetian blind. A real panel is 6-9 cells across.

roughness.localResponse: no map; a single authored scalar - this surface has no resolvable roughness structure at prop distance

Never alias albedo into roughness; both are authored scalars, not maps.

materials.notes: Roughness 0.30 -- a glazed laminate, the smoothest surface on the prop.

If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.

AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 1.340 x 4.546 x 0.716 m against the declared 1.35 x 4.6 x 0.75 -- within 1% on width, 1.2% on height and 4.5% on depth. Width is the panel's -X overhang plus the lamp head's +X, which is exactly how the asset notes describe the figure.

A 0.92 x 0.74 m laminate raked 0.30 rad in an aluminium frame that stands proud of it on all four sides, with the cell grid as a post-construction tile. The previous build was a bare flat plate with no cells, no frame and no strut. Panel 0.74 deep rather than the notes' rough 0.6: the declared envelope depth is 0.75 and the panel is the only thing that can set it -- at 0.6 the measured depth came out 12% under.

A flat slab head with a darker lens plate, on a short arm on the OPPOSITE side of the pole from the panel and 0.64 m below it. The asset notes make exactly that arrangement the identity -- 'those two must stay separate volumes at the right relative sizes' -- and it is now legible from every azimuth.

Two material layers: galvanised steel for pole, gussets, plate, mount and head, and a PV laminate carrying its aluminium frame as a vertex colour. Galvanised luma 162 is clear of the 55.5-60.5 window gatecrop's alpha key erases. The cell tile was rescaled from 0.16 m to 0.55 m: at 0.16 it repeated six times across the panel and its bands read as a venetian blind rather than the 6-9 cells a real panel has. NOT carried: the plate's heavy rust bleed at the foot, which is directional where the tile is isotropic.

A flared foot at r 0.088 tapering to r 0.038 at the head, with four triangular gussets welded up from the baseplate and four bolts on a 0.32 m plate. The previous build was a smooth pipe with none of it; the gussets are what read as a bolted structural post rather than a tube pushed into a plate.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Raised to hero with the lighting kit and heavily underspent: 420 triangles at 5 draw calls, 2 materials and 5 geometries. The prop is boxes and one lathe, so the triangle ceiling was never the constraint -- the draw calls are, and 5 of 6 is the real cost of keeping the panel, its mount and the head as the separate volumes the asset notes require.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A soft key from the upper front-left; the pole's left facets read brighter than its right and the panel's glazing catches the brightest highlight.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review harness parity - the harness key sits at (3, 5, 4).

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Shadow sides lifted rather than black, roughly a 0.7 shadow-to-key ratio.
No separate rim in the plate - the object separates from the backdrop by value alone.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review only; the harness rim at (0, 3, -5) is a harness convention the model must not depend on.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A pure white seamless backdrop at luma ~255; foreground coverage is 20.5%. The review harness approximates it with a HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x404040, 1.6) and NO environment map, which is why every metal here is authored below metalness 1.0: a raw metal has no diffuse term and nothing to reflect, and it renders DARKER than the 58 backdrop, which the turntable gate reads as a hole punched through the model.

The review harness applies ACES filmic tone mapping, which rolls off highlights, so a painted luma reads lower than its raw value. Albedo is therefore verified in the render and corrected against the measurement rather than copied through from the crop.

Ambient occlusion is authored per material (cavityStrength 0.2, contactShadowBias 0.3) to darken joints and seams. The prop's ground shadow is the level bake's job, not the factory's - the factory sets castShadow/receiveShadow and nothing else.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.

pivots.name: Base centre
pivots.rationale: The ONLY pivot. The panel is aimed once at installation, which is a siting choice and not a runtime mechanism, so it gets no axis of its own.

animationAnchors.socketsRationale: NONE, deliberately. Nothing clips onto this prop; the panel and lamp box are fixed to their own pole.

destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
